findings.title: The `step()` code skips `post_tick()` when there are no entities, which the doc says must not happen
findings.description: The `step()` code under Implementation Details (lines 276-277) returns early with `if self._entity_manager.count == 0: return`. That return comes before `self._environment.post_tick()`. The note right after it (line 291), and Special Considerations (line 408), both say `post_tick()` must still run with zero entities, and that "the early return is moved to wrap only `engine.tick()`." The earlier version in "SimulationManager as Simulation Orchestrator" (lines 180-190) gets this right by putting `tick()` inside an `if count > 0:` block. The two snippets disagree, and the one under Implementation Details is the one an implementer is most likely to copy. Fix: remove the early-return version and keep the guarded-block form. Add a success criterion that `post_tick` is called when the entity count is zero.

findings.title: Scope the slice plan gives to 304 is dropped or deferred without saying so
findings.description:
The slice plan entry (300-slices line 27) gives 304 these jobs:
- environment configuration with "seed, grid resolution, layer selection"
- "Handle post-tick environment writes (e.g., stigmergic trail deposits)"

Entry 305 (line 29) also says "Terrain summary in snapshots deferred to (304)." This design:
- Excludes grid resolution and layer selection (line 48, line 153).
- Moves environment data in snapshots to unnamed "future work" (line 47), so the item 305 handed to 304 now has no owner.
- Calls `post_tick()` with no arguments (lines 105, 190). It gives no path for collecting `trail_deposits` or `threat_mutations` from the engine and passing them to `Environment.post_tick(trail_deposits, threat_mutations)` (500-slice lines 284-290; 500-arch line 83).

Some of these deferrals make sense while no layers exist. But the slice plan is not updated, and no slice is named to take each item. Fix: either name the slice that owns each item (for example 501 for grid resolution, 506 for trail-deposit plumbing, a named slice for the snapshot terrain summary) and update the slice plan, or deliver them here.

findings.title: Environment context is not passed to `engine.tick()`, which departs from the architecture and the slice plan without saying so
findings.description:
Several documents expect the environment to go to the engine at tick time:
- The 300-arch tick cycle (step 3): "Pass current entity state and environment context to the behavior engine."
- The slice plan: "Pass environment context to `SimulationManager` and `engine.tick()`."
- 500-arch line 52 and 500-slice line 422: the world server passes the environment (or its `query` method) to `engine.tick()`.

This design instead uses constructor injection into forces and leaves `tick(...)` unchanged (lines 279-285). That is a reasonable, lighter choice, because it needs no change to the `BulkForce` protocol. But it changes the integration contract that initiatives 100 and 500 are coding against, and the doc doesn't flag that. Fix: state the decision as an explicit deviation and record it in the 300 slice plan and the 500 integration notes. Otherwise behavior-engine slices will expect a `tick()` parameter that never arrives.

findings.title: "Environment is Always Present" contradicts the `Environment | None` design
findings.description:
This section says the always-present environment "avoids `if environment is not None:` checks scattered through the codebase." The same design still:
- types the parameter as `Environment | None = None` (line 263)
- exposes `environment -> Environment | None` (line 269)
- adds two `None` checks in `step()` (lines 273, 287)

The only reason given is that existing tests don't pass an environment. `Environment(bounds, layers={})` is cheap to build (500-slice walkthrough step 6). Making the parameter required removes both branches and the optional property, and every future force builder then gets a non-optional type. Fix: make `environment` required and update the existing SimulationManager tests to pass an empty `Environment`.

findings.title: Hard-coded seed and seasonal defaults, with conflicting descriptions
findings.description:
Project rules forbid silent fallbacks and magic defaults outside config, and the doc has several:
- `seed: int = 42` is used quietly when the section is missing (lines 149-151, 231).
- `step()` hard-codes `seasonal_parameter: float = 0.0` as a default argument in simulation code, not config (lines 176, 272).
- State Management lists a `_seasonal_parameter: float` attribute (line 119), but no code ever stores or reads it. This leaves it unclear whether the value lives on the instance or in the argument.
- Line 198 calls 0.0 a "mid-season" environment. On the continuous 0–1 cycle defined in the slice plan (entry 308), that wording doesn't match 0.0.

Fix:
- Have `server.py` pass the seasonal value in explicitly, with no default argument, until slice 308 supplies real values.
- Remove the unused `_seasonal_parameter` attribute.
- Either make `seed` required whenever the `environment` section is present, or log the default seed at INFO when it is used.
- Fix the "mid-season" wording.

findings.title: No defined behavior when `pre_tick()` or `post_tick()` raises inside the tick body
findings.description: This slice adds two new calls into another subsystem on every tick. `Environment.pre_tick()` is documented to raise `ValueError` when `seasonal_parameter` is outside [0, 1] (500-slice lines 277-281, 445). Future layers can raise from `pre_tick` or `post_tick` as well. The design doesn't say what the tick loop does with that exception: crash the server, log and skip the tick, or something else. It also doesn't say whether a failed `pre_tick` should stop `engine.tick` from running against a half-updated environment. The 301 tick-loop design has no exception-handling rule to fall back on. The architecture's "Explicit lifecycle … No silent failures, no undefined states" (300-arch line 45) requires this to be defined. Fix: state the policy (for example, a raise from either call ends the tick and the exception goes to the server's top-level handler, logged at ERROR, and the server shuts down). Add a test that asserts that outcome.

findings.title: The tick-budget requirement is not restated even though this slice changes the hot tick path
findings.description: The 300 architecture sets target tick rates of 20–60 Hz (a 16.7–50 ms budget) and an operating range of 10K–50K entities (300-arch lines 78, 94). This slice adds two calls to every tick in `SimulationManager.step()`, but Success Criteria and Technical Requirements don't mention the budget. Fix: restate the target, for example "with an empty environment, the added `pre_tick`/`post_tick` overhead is negligible against the 50 ms budget at 20 Hz with the default population; overruns are still reported by the 301 tick metrics."

findings.title: Future environment-aware forces will fail if any entity drifts outside world bounds
findings.description: In the illustrative `TerrainResistance`, `self._environment.query(state.positions)` runs on every entity position. `Environment.query()` rejects the whole batch with `ValueError` if any position is out of bounds (500-slice lines 322-333). Neither 303 nor this slice keeps entities inside the world bounds. This slice builds no forces, so it's not a blocker. But the "environment available for forces" value it claims depends on an entity-boundary policy that no slice owns yet. Name it as a prerequisite for the first force that uses the environment.

findings.title: `WorldBounds` is called "shared with entity manager," but `EntityManager` receives the config type
findings.description: `EntityManager.__init__` receives `world_bounds` from `SimulationConfig`, which is a `WorldBoundsConfig` (303-slice lines 98, 283). It does not receive the new `WorldBounds` instance. Either reword the line, or pass the converted `WorldBounds` to `EntityManager` too, so there is a single source for the coordinate system.

findings.title: Seed validation accepts booleans
findings.description: The rule "`seed` must be an int if present" will accept `seed: true` when checked with `isinstance(x, int)`, because Python's `bool` is a subclass of `int`. Say that bool is rejected, and include that case in the config validation tests.

findings.title: The slice keeps the server as orchestrator and puts the two-phase calls in the right order
findings.description: The order `pre_tick` → `engine.tick` → `post_tick` matches the two-phase protocol and the "immutable during evaluation" rule in 500-arch (lines 55-60), and fixes the old single `environment.update()` call in the slice plan. The server only builds and calls the `Environment`. It reimplements no layer logic, which fits "Orchestrator, not monolith" and the integration-slice pattern in the slice-plan notes. Dependency direction is correct: `migratory_server` depends on `migratory.environment`, with nothing going the other way.
